title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: The boy took his sheep to a green hill near the village.
The first time, the villagers came with sticks and tools.
The first time the boy shouted, a wolf was chasing the sheep.
The villagers thought the boy's joke was funny.
One afternoon, a real wolf came out of the forest.
When the real wolf came, the villagers ran to help.
How did the boy sometimes feel on the hill?
What were the sheep doing when the villagers arrived?
What did one man say to the boy?
items.why: "That is not funny," one man said.

items.q: Why did nobody come the last time?
options: They thought he was trying to fool them again
items.why: "He is trying to fool us again," they said.

items.q: What happens when we tell lies, says the story?
items.why: “When we tell lies, people stop believing us.”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: A shepherd boy shouted "Wolf!" two times as a joke, and the villagers ran to help him. When a real wolf came, he shouted again, but nobody believed him. The wolf chased the sheep away, and the boy learned that people stop believing us when we tell lies.

items.q: Why did the boy shout "Wolf!" when there was no wolf?
items.model: He was bored, and he wanted to fool the villagers. He laughed when they came.

items.q: What did the villagers do the second time?
items.model: They ran up the hill again, but there was no wolf. They shook their heads and went home.

items.q: What did the boy understand at the end?
items.model: When we tell lies, people stop believing us.

items.q: Why is it important to tell the truth?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the events in the order of the story.
items: The boy became bored on the hill
The villagers ran up the hill, but there was no wolf
The boy did it again a few days later
A real wolf came out of the forest
The wolf chased the sheep away
